top_story: The 30 September U.S. bombing of Shajareh Tayyebeh School in Minab, followed by 2 October testimony and video from survivors and first responders, has fixed the strike in public view as a mass-casualty trauma likely to deepen Iranian anger well beyond state channels and harden regional perceptions of unchecked U.S. violence. That civilian toll gives sharper political charge to a second aviation-linked security shock: the alleged 1 October stabbing by an Omani co-pilot on a Dubai–Tel Aviv Flydubai flight, which by 2 October had moved into direct Israeli questioning and Netanyahu’s effort to frame the episode as Islamist radicalization. Together, the incidents tighten a regional atmosphere in which civilian spaces—schools and commercial aircraft—are recast as sites of war and ideological threat, increasing fear among ordinary people while giving governments wider room to securitize travel, dissent, and cross-border contact.
